topics.title: Were the revolutions of 1848 important?

outcomes.text: Explain how liberal and nationalist ideas grew in influence before 1848.
Explain why so many revolutions broke out across Europe in 1848.
Identify what the 1848 revolutions had in common.
Describe causes, events and results of the 1848 revolution in France.
Describe causes, events and results of the 1848 revolutions in Italy.
Describe causes, events and results of the 1848 revolutions in Germany.
Describe causes, events and results of the 1848 revolutions in the Austrian Empire.
Explain why most 1848 revolutions failed.
Judge whether the revolutions changed anything.

topics.title: How was Italy unified?

outcomes.text: Describe Austrian influence over Italy.
Explain Italian nationalism and Mazzini's role.
Explain why Italy was not unified in 1848-49 and what happened in those years.
Explain the Plombieres agreement and the 1859 war with Austria.
Assess whether Cavour helped or hindered unification.
Describe Garibaldi's invasion of Sicily and Naples and judge its importance.
Describe the creation of the Kingdom of Italy and completion of unification by 1870.
Explain the importance of Italian unification for other European countries.

topics.title: How was Germany unified?

outcomes.text: Explain German nationalism and the role of the Zollverein.
Describe the 1848 revolution in Prussia and the Frankfurt Parliament's rise and failure.
Explain how Austrian influence in Germany was re-established by 1850.

subtopics.title: Bismarck and the defeat of Austria

outcomes.text: Describe Bismarck's rise as Prussian Minister-President.
Explain the Schleswig-Holstein question and the Austro-Prussian War and its consequences.

subtopics.title: Bismarck and the defeat of France

outcomes.text: Explain relations with France, the Spanish Succession and the Franco-Prussian War.
Describe the creation of the German empire.
Judge how far Bismarck was responsible for German unification.

topics.title: Why was there a civil war in the United States and what were its results?

outcomes.text: Compare the North and South before the war.
Explain slavery, slave and free states, and abolitionism.
Explain the significance of Lincoln's 1860 election and Southern secession.
Explain why the North won and the South lost, and the role of Lincoln.
Describe Reconstruction and how far it succeeded.

topics.title: Why, and with what effects, did nations gain and expand their overseas empires in the nineteenth century?

outcomes.text: Explain economic, military, geopolitical, religious and cultural motives for imperialism.
Describe French assimilation and direct rule, with Faidherbe and Senegal.
Describe British indirect rule, with Lugard and Nigeria.
Describe Leopold II's private imperialism in the Congo and its effects.
Explain the events of 1857 and how they changed British rule in India.
Explain the wars of independence in the Philippines and Cuba, the Spanish-American War and the Treaty of Paris.
Describe the US debate over imperialism.
Describe the effects of American control on the Philippines and US intervention in Cuba to 1906.

topics.title: What caused the First World War?

outcomes.text: Explain how the Alliance System shaped European diplomacy.
Explain the 1902 Anglo-Japanese Alliance.
Explain the arms race.
Explain how colonial rivalries created tension between Great Powers.
Explain developments in the Balkans and why they were hard to solve.
Explain how the June-July 1914 crisis led to war.

topics.title: Was the Treaty of Versailles fair?

outcomes.text: Explain the roles and aims of Wilson, Clemenceau and Lloyd George.
Explain why the victors did not get everything they wanted.

subtopics.title: Terms and impact of the Treaty

outcomes.text: Describe the terms of the Treaty.
Describe its social, economic and political impact on Germany to 1923.
Explain contemporary opinions about the Treaty and whether it could be justified.

topics.title: To what extent was the League of Nations a success?

outcomes.text: Describe the League's structure, aims and membership.
Explain how organisational and membership weaknesses made failure likely.
Assess League action in Vilna, Aaland Islands, Corfu and Bulgaria.
Describe League work on refugees, health, working conditions and slavery.
Explain how the Depression made the League's work harder.
Explain the causes, events and consequences of the Manchurian and Abyssinian crises.

topics.title: How far was Hitler's foreign policy to blame for the outbreak of war in Europe in 1939?

outcomes.text: Describe Hitler's foreign policy aims and rearmament.
Explain long-term consequences of Versailles and the Saar and Rhineland events.
Explain the Rome-Berlin Axis and Anti-Comintern Pact.
Describe German and Italian involvement in the Spanish Civil War.
Explain the Anschluss with Austria.
Explain the Czechoslovakia crisis and Munich Agreement, and whether appeasement was justified.
Explain the Nazi-Soviet Pact's importance.
Explain the Polish crisis and why Britain and France declared war.

topics.title: Who was to blame for the Cold War?

outcomes.text: Explain the 1945 summit conferences and breakdown of the US-Soviet alliance in 1945-46.
Describe Soviet control of Eastern Europe to 1948 and the American reaction.
Describe the occupation of Germany and the Berlin Blockade.
Explain the formation of NATO and the Warsaw Pact.
Judge whether the USA or USSR was more to blame.

topics.title: How effectively did the United States contain the spread of communism?

outcomes.text: Describe American reactions to North Korea's invasion, the UN role and the war to 1953.
Describe American reactions to the Cuban Revolution, the Missile Crisis and its aftermath.
Explain reasons for American involvement in Vietnam.
Describe American tactics and strategy in Vietnam.
Explain the reasons for American withdrawal.

topics.title: How secure was the USSR's control over Eastern Europe, 1948-c.1989?

outcomes.text: Explain resistance to Soviet power in Hungary in 1956 and the Soviet reaction.
Explain resistance in Czechoslovakia in 1968 and compare it with Hungary.
Explain why the Berlin Wall was built in 1961.
Explain the significance of Solidarity in Poland.
Judge Gorbachev's responsibility for the collapse of Soviet control.

units.title: Depth study A: The First World War, 1914-18

topics.title: Why was there stalemate on the Western Front?

outcomes.text: Explain how the Schlieffen Plan worked, including Belgium, the BEF and Russian mobilisation.
Describe Mons, the Marne, the race to the sea and First Ypres, and the emergence of attrition.
Describe the nature and problems of trench warfare.
Assess the impact of tanks, machine guns, aircraft and gas.
Explain the impact of Verdun and the Somme, including Haig's leadership and tactics.

topics.title: To what extent was it a world war?

outcomes.text: Describe the role and experiences of British Empire troops on the Western Front, including Indian and Canadian troops.
Describe the war in German East Africa and South West Africa.
Explain Japan's contribution, including Tsingtao and naval assistance.
Explain the importance of the Arab Revolt.

topics.title: How important were other fronts?

outcomes.text: Explain the Battle of Jutland and its consequences.
Explain convoys, submarines and the U-boat campaign.
Explain the reasons for and results of the Gallipoli campaign.
Describe events on the Eastern Front and the defeat of Russia.
Describe the impact of war on civilian populations.

topics.title: Why did Germany ask for an armistice in 1918?

outcomes.text: Explain the impact of American entry into the war.
Explain the German offensive of 1918 and the Allied advance.
Describe conditions in Germany late in the war, the Kiel Mutiny and German Revolution.
Explain the Kaiser's abdication and why the Armistice was signed.

topics.title: Was the Weimar Republic doomed from the start?

outcomes.text: Describe the Revolution of 1918 and establishment of the Republic.
Explain the Versailles Settlement and German reactions to it.
Explain the Weimar Constitution, political divisions and the army's role.
Describe threats from left and right in 1919-23.
Explain hyper-inflation and the Ruhr occupation.
Assess Stresemann's economic and foreign policy achievements.
Describe the cultural achievements of the Weimar period.

topics.title: Why was Hitler able to dominate Germany by 1934?

outcomes.text: Explain Nazi ideas and methods in the 1920s.
Describe the Munich Putsch and the roles of Hitler and other leaders.
Explain the political, economic and social crisis of 1930-33.
Explain the reasons for the Nazis' rise and how Hitler took power.
Explain the Reichstag Fire and the 1933 election.
Explain the Enabling Act, Night of the Long Knives and Hindenburg's death.

topics.title: The Nazi regime

outcomes.text: Explain removal of opposition and methods of control and repression.
Explain use of culture and mass media.
Assess opposition to Nazi rule.
Describe anti-Semitism and persecution of minorities.
Explain Nazi economic policy including rearmament.
Describe the experiences of women and young people.
Explain how war changed life, including the war economy and the Final Solution.

topics.title: Why did the Tsarist regime collapse in 1917?

outcomes.text: Describe the main features of Tsarist rule and Russian society before the war.
Explain the 1905 Revolution, its aftermath and attempts at reform.
Explain the First World War's impact on the Russian people.
Explain why the March Revolution of 1917 succeeded.

topics.title: How did the Bolsheviks gain power, and how did they consolidate their rule?

outcomes.text: Explain the Provisional Government, the Soviets and rising revolutionary groups.
Explain why the Provisional Government failed.
Describe the Bolshevik seizure of power and Lenin's role.
Describe Bolshevik rule, the Civil War, War Communism and why the Bolsheviks won.
Explain the Kronstadt Rising and the New Economic Policy.

topics.title: How did Stalin gain and hold on to power?

outcomes.text: Describe Lenin's death and the struggle for power.
Explain why Stalin became leader by 1928.
Explain Stalin's use of terror and the Purges.
Explain propaganda and official culture.

topics.title: What was the impact of Stalin's economic policies?

outcomes.text: Explain modernisation of Soviet industry and the Five-Year Plans.
Explain collectivisation in agriculture.
Describe the differing experiences of social groups, ethnic minorities and women.

units.title: Depth study D: The United States, 1919-41

topics.title: How far did the US economy boom in the 1920s?

outcomes.text: Explain government policies and mass production of cars and consumer goods.
Explain credit and hire purchase.
Describe the fortunes of older industries and the decline of agriculture.
Identify weaknesses in the economy by the late 1920s.

topics.title: How far did US society change in the 1920s?

outcomes.text: Describe the Roaring Twenties, film and other media.
Describe the changing roles of women.
Explain Prohibition and gangsterism.
Explain immigration restrictions, the Red Scare and religious intolerance.
Explain discrimination against Black Americans and the Ku Klux Klan.

topics.title: What were the causes and consequences of the Wall Street Crash?

outcomes.text: Explain the Wall Street Crash and its financial, economic and social effects.
Describe Hoover's reaction to the Crash.
Compare Hoover's and Roosevelt's 1932 programmes and explain Roosevelt's win.

topics.title: How successful was the New Deal?

outcomes.text: Describe Roosevelt's inauguration and the Hundred Days.
Describe New Deal legislation, the alphabet agencies and the changes they caused.
Explain opposition from Republicans, the rich, business, the Supreme Court and Huey Long.
Assess the New Deal's strengths and weaknesses on unemployment and the Depression.

units.title: Depth study E: The Second World War in Europe and the Asia-Pacific, 1939-c.1945

topics.title: How did the Second World War in Europe develop?

outcomes.text: Describe the fall of France and the Vichy government, and Dunkirk.
Explain Operation Sea Lion and the Battle of Britain.
Explain Operation Barbarossa and early Nazi successes.
Explain the German defeat at Stalingrad and its impact.

topics.title: How did the Second World War in the Asia-Pacific develop?

outcomes.text: Explain reasons for the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor and its consequences.
Explain Japanese successes in Southeast Asia by 1942, with Malaya and Singapore.
Explain the Battle of Midway and its impact.

topics.title: What was the impact of war on civilian populations in Europe and the Asia-Pacific?

outcomes.text: Describe the Blitz and Allied bombing of German cities and their effects on morale.
Describe the impact of Japanese control in Malaya and Singapore.
Describe Nazi control in Poland, leading to the Holocaust.
Assess the methods and effectiveness of resistance in Malaya and France.

topics.title: How did the Allies achieve victory over the Axis powers?

outcomes.text: Describe the Allied invasion of Sicily and victory in Italy.
Explain the D-Day landings, advance to Germany and the Russian advance.
Explain Guadalcanal, Okinawa and island-hopping.
Explain the bombing of Japan and the decision to use the atomic bomb.
Describe the Allied occupations of Germany and Japan.
Describe the Nuremberg and Tokyo war crimes trials.
